# ABSTRACT

Printed circuit board (PCB) schematic design defines nearly all electronic hardware, but it remains mostly manual and expertise-intensive. While generative AI has advanced digital and analog IC design, PCB schematic generation from natural-language intent is largely unexplored. This paper presents [NAME C08], a large language model that generates editable PCB schematics from natural-language requests. The key challenge lies in the lack of an LLM-suited representation and a large-scale dataset. Current schematic formats are dominated by verbose, tool-specific syntax and geometry-heavy descriptions, making them difficult to generate reliably. We introduce a semantically grounded code representation that encodes schematic editing primitives with relative placement and pin-name-based wiring, transforming a geometry-driven generation problem into a semantics-driven matching task amenable to LLMs. We further construct a large-scale dataset of PCB schematics paired with user prompts via a human-agent collaborative pipeline that converts open-source hardware designs into our representation. ### 3.3 FINE-TUNING AND PROMPTED GENERATION

We separately fine-tune GPT-oss-20b and Qwen3.8-27B to generate schematic construction programs from natural-language requests. Both backbones use the same underlying request–program pairs, but receive backbone-specific synthetic chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision. Specifically, each backbone generates CoT traces for its own training examples, and these traces are incorporated into the corresponding training sequences. The CoT tokens contribute to the supervised training loss, providing explicit supervision for intermediate reasoning alongside schematic program generation.

At inference time, each model produces a construction program in a single generation attempt, after which the program is executed to obtain an editable schematic with no iterative generation or execution-feedback repair applied. Detailed training settings are provided in Section 6.5.

## AI USE STATEMENT

We used LLMs to assist with language and LaTeX polishing, synthetic dataset construction. The authors take full responsibility for the final manuscript, methods, results, and claims.

## ETHICS STATEMENT

[NAME C08] aims to make PCB schematic design more accessible, while recognizing that errors in generated circuits can cause hardware failures or physical harm. The reported execution checks, connectivity metrics, and expert assessments do not establish safety or reliability in physical deployment. Generated designs therefore require qualified engineering review and application-appropriate electrical validation before fabrication or use, particularly in safety-critical settings. The dataset is derived from publicly available hardware designs, including SparkFun designs described in the paper as licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0; redistribution of source and derived assets must preserve applicable attribution and license obligations.
